study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
exposure: Elective induction of labor (EIOL) start time (categorized as early a.m., late AM, early p.m., or late p.m.)
cohort: Low-risk nulliparous women undergoing elective induction of labor between 39 0/7 and 39 4/7 weeks gestation, who did not experience spontaneous labor or rupture of membranes prior to induction.
finding: Induction of labor starting between 6 a.m. and 11:59 a.m. (late a.m.) was significantly associated with shorter labor durations.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates did not differ by the start time of elective induction of labor.
